panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Clinical photograph of a 4-year-old girl with JDM showing periorbital edema with hyperpigmentation (heliotrope rash), a classic cutaneous manifestation. Eyes blacked out for privacy. B: Clinical photograph showing an ecthyma-like ulcer on the shoulder from calcified nodules that expelled calcified material (calcinosis cutis), plus nonscarring alopecia, in a child with JDM. C: Clinical photograph showing a hyperpigmented rash on the neck in a child with JDM; a real cutaneous manifestation but no specific vocabulary key, so recorded as a proposed finding. D: Clinical photograph showing calcified papules and nodules around the knee with chalky extrusion of calcified material, classic calcinosis cutis in JDM. E: Clinical photograph showing small flat-topped papules over the interphalangeal joints, captioned as possible early Gottron's papules, a classic JDM finding.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal knee MRI in a patient with juvenile dermatomyositis (article title: tumoral calcinoosis of the knee with secondary infection in juvenile dermatomyositis). White arrows point to lobulated hypointense calcified masses in the anterior soft tissues, i.e., dystrophic calcinosis, with associated fascial thickening/edema described in the text. Calcinoosis is a recognized, less common complication of juvenile dermatomyositis, so attribution and findings are well supported. B: Sagittal knee MRI in the same juvenile dermatomyositis patient. White arrows indicate lobulated hypointense calcified masses anterior to the knee joint (tumoral/dystrophic calcinosis), with the text describing surrounding hyperintense inflammatory change, fascial thickening and a suprapatellar fluid collection. Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title plus the captioned calcification manifestation.
